Nell describes Emily’s offer of help as “a coat draped over your shoulders that you never agreed to wear,” capturing its simultaneous comfort and burden. Emily’s love becomes “ferocity aimed at a target she considers worth the ammunition,” revealing care expressed through force. Recurring financial language—“small surrenders,” “investment,” and “every ledger in the world”—also connects economic worth with Nell’s struggle to preserve a self that cannot be priced.
